messages:
cheng: Heads-up — after last night's runtime roll (kernel selector -> fused-attn-v2 + batch heuristic tweak) we're seeing a sustained drop in prefix/KV cache hit rate for several hosted models. Link: https://dash.redwood/internal/kvcache?run=2026-07-11
eva: On it. How big is the hit?
perf-bot: KV cache hit-rate (p50) changed from 72.3% -> 44.9% across models gpt-small-*; tail latency +35ms. (metrics snapshot)
```
model,gold_hit,post_roll
'gpt-small-v1',0.723,0.449
'gpt-rt-quant',0.695,0.421
```
sam: That's huge. Any correlation with batch size distribution or kernel flags?
cheng: We profiled; the kernel swap introduced a different key hash path. Previously we used Murmur3(seed=0); new fused kernel calls into runtime::hash_key() which mixes in 'kernel-feature-bit' -> effectively a salt.

`diff --git a/hash.cc b/hash.cc ... +mix(seed, flags)`

This means cached keys for identical prompts no longer match.
marco: Wait, is the salt per-worker or per-process? If per-worker then warmup will diverge and some workers never see warm cache.
cheng: It's per-process (set at init from kernel selection). So warmup that hits older workers > doesn't match new ones; we get shard-local misses.
jyoti: Could quant profile change amplify this (different token lengths, KV shape)? We saw minor seq-len shift but not big enough to explain 25-30% drop.
sam: Repro steps I ran locally: `curl -X POST https://local-runtime:8080/generate -d @prompt.json -H 'X-KV-Warmup: true'`; before roll -> 0.78 hit, after roll -> 0.46. Paste logs:
```
[2026-07-11T02:12:03Z] warmup: key=0x7fabc123 hit=true
[2026-07-11T02:12:03Z] warmup: key=0x8ccdff00 hit=false (new hash)
```
eva: Short-term mitigation: normalize hash by stripping kernel-bit before key lookup. Can we patch runtime quickly? Risk: perf of key comparison may change.
cheng: I opened a rollback PR for the kernel selector as contingency: https://git.redwood/repo/pulls/3921
sam: Long-term: make cache key include explicit kernel version string in metadata and use canonicalization for lookup; or use distributed key migration tool to re-warm new-worker caches.
marco: Also add a warmup fanout to ensure all workers get same keys post-deploy.
jyoti: I can run a trace to confirm per-worker hit variance; need sample prompt set. Cheng — can you push the top-50 warmup prompts to /tmp/kv-warmup-sample.json?
cheng: done: /tmp/kv-warmup-sample.json (pushed to infra-storage). I'm running the trace now and will attach results.
perf-bot: Trace started. expected finish in ~6m.
cheng: Quick note — this explains why Dedicated customers with long-lived workers didn't see as big a regression; their workers kept old seed. Also explains region variance.
eva: Ok, action items: (1) revert kernel selector if rollback green (cheng), (2) hotfix to canonicalize keys (sam), (3) run distributed warmup tool with sample set (marco), (4) postmortem doc (jyoti). ETA EOD. :thumbsup:
sam: I'll open the hotfix PR and bench key-lookup cost before merge.
cheng: Thanks all. I'll dump per-worker hit histograms once trace finishes.
